summary:
ITM 2026, held in Istanbul alongside HIGHTEX 2026, welcomed 48,257 professional visitors from 105 countries and featured over 1,000 exhibitors from 59 nations.
The exhibition generated strong machinery sales, investment discussions and international partnerships.
Sustainability, automation, digitalisation and AI-driven textile technologies emerged as key areas of visitor interest.

title: China’s Hainan Free Trade Port sees 120% rise in zero-tariff imports
summary:
Hainan Free Trade Port’s zero-tariff imports surged 120 per cent to 2.65 billion yuan after island-wide customs reforms launched on December 18. 
Total trade rose 54.6 per cent, supported by faster clearance, expanded tariff exemptions, and growing enterprise registrations, highlighting strong momentum in the region’s opening-up and industrial expansion.

title: US, Iran sign pact to end Middle East conflict
summary:
Presidents Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian have signed a pact to end the Middle East conflict and revive talks on Iran’s nuclear programme. 
Tehran will reduce its enriched uranium in return for relief from US sanctions. 
The deal comes into force immediately and sets a 60-day timeline for talks on a long-term settlement. 
Iran can resume unrestricted oil exports and the Strait of Hormuz will reopen.

title: Naphtha prices ease further, offering cost relief to textile producers
summary:
Global naphtha prices fell sharply in early June as lower crude oil costs, improved supply availability and easing geopolitical tensions reduced pressure across petrochemical markets.
Prices declined by over 10 per cent week on week and more than 30 per cent from mid-May levels in key Asian markets.
Softer naphtha costs may ease input expenses for polyester and synthetic fibre producers.

title: Trump, Modi call for commercially meaningful bilateral trade pact
summary:
PM Narendra Modi yesterday met President Donald Trump on the margins of the G7 Summit in Evian, and both instructed their officials to work towards a balanced, mutually-beneficial and commercially meaningful bilateral trade pact.
USTR Jamieson Greer will visit India next week in this connection.
Modi also met top EU leaders, and they stressed on the quick signing and implementation of the India-EU FTA.

title: India-UK trade pact to enter into force on July 15
summary:
Indian PM Narendra Modi has expressed delight that the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement will enter into force on July 15.
“This agreement will significantly boost our bilateral trade and investment,” he said.
He met UK PM Keir Starmer on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Evian, and both reaffirmed shared commitment to further strengthen the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

title: Euro area labour costs rise 3.2% in Q1; EU records 3.6% increase
summary:
Hourly labour costs increased 3.2 per cent year on year in the euro area and 3.6 per cent in the EU in Q1 2026, driven by higher wage and non-wage expenses. 
Construction recorded the strongest growth among major sectors, while Hungary, Bulgaria, and Croatia posted the largest increases in hourly wage costs across member states, Eurostat reported.

title: Euro area economic index drops 0.3% in May amid weak sentiment: TCB
summary:
The Conference Board’s Leading Economic Index (LEI) for the Euro area fell 0.3 per cent in May 2026, marking its third consecutive monthly decline and signalling continued pressure on economic activity. 
Weak consumer, services and industrial-sector expectations weighed on the index. 
However, financial indicators helped limit the decline. 
It forecasts Euro area real GDP growth of 1 per cent in 2026.

title: Industrial production inches higher across EU, Euro area in April
summary:
Industrial production in both the euro area and the EU rose 0.1 per cent in April 2026 from March, while increasing 0.3 per cent and 0.9 per cent year on year, respectively.
Growth was driven by non-durable consumer goods and intermediate goods. 
Malta, Sweden and the Netherlands recorded the strongest monthly gains, while Denmark led annual growth at 12.2 per cent.

title: Ozempic is creating a new wardrobe economy
summary:
Rising GLP-1 use is reshaping apparel demand by accelerating size changes and wardrobe replacement.
The challenge for brands is not simply stocking smaller sizes but adapting sizing, inventory and product design to changing body measurements.
Dynamic size planning, fit-based data and transitional garments will be essential to reduce returns, avoid inventory mismatches and capture new demand.

title: Morocco's apparel exports fall 8% in Q1 2026; Spain remains top market
summary:

Spain remained the largest destination, accounting for over 63 per cent of exports.
Despite the quarterly decline, annual apparel exports rose to $3.94 billion in 2025, highlighting the sector's long-term growth.

title: UK’s clothing exports down 3% to $299 mn in April 2026
summary:

Textile fabric and fibre exports also declined.
In Q1 2026, clothing exports dropped 7.87 per cent, extending a broader downward trend seen since 2023, while upstream segments showed relative resilience.

title: EU ban turns unsold fashion stock into auditable business risk in 2026
summary:
The EU’s July 2026 ban on destroying unsold apparel, footwear and accessories transforms excess inventory into a measurable compliance and financial risk.
Combined with EPR obligations and disclosure requirements, the rules push brands to improve forecasting, inventory management, resale and recycling strategies, making overproduction increasingly costly and difficult to justify.

title: UK summerwear imports rise ahead of weather-driven demand
summary:
UK retailers increased imports of summer apparel ahead of the spring heatwave, indicating proactive demand planning rather than reactive buying.
Growth was strongest in T-shirts, shorts and lightweight clothing, while sportswear lagged.
The trend highlights the importance of agile sourcing, seasonal relevance and competitive pricing in a cautious consumer environment.

title: India's textile, apparel exports fall 4.4% in April-May
summary:
India's textile and apparel exports fell 4.44 per cent year on year (YoY) to $5.91 billion in April-May FY27, dragged down by a 12.98 per cent decline in apparel shipments despite a 3.03 per cent rise in textile exports.
Weak Middle East demand and a high base impacted apparel export, while cotton imports surged and textile imports remained subdued.

title: IAF launches manifesto for smart, sustainable apparel manufacturing
summary:
IAF’s new manifesto urges apparel manufacturers and brands to move beyond lowest-cost sourcing and focus on end-to-end productivity, demand alignment and supply chain resilience. 
It highlights smart flexibility, stronger textile-apparel collaboration and lower inventory risk. 
The roadmap centres on defining shared goals, enabling innovation and standardising scalable industry practices.

title: India’s green manufacturing push: Solar farms to net zero
summary:
Indian apparel manufacturers are embedding sustainability into factory design, energy sourcing and production processes to meet evolving global compliance requirements.
Investments in renewable energy, net-zero facilities and climate-resilient infrastructure are accelerating, while heat stress mitigation and decarbonisation are emerging as critical priorities for long-term competitiveness.

title: UK’s clothing imports up 2.4% to $1.8 bn in April 2026
summary:

However, January-March imports fell 3 per cent from a year earlier.
Despite the quarterly slowdown, clothing imports increased 6.1 per cent to £17.73 billion in 2025, highlighting resilient consumer demand.

title: Bangladesh-US apparel paradox shows higher rank and weaker momentum
summary:
Bangladesh remains the second-largest apparel supplier to the US, but exports are losing momentum despite China’s sharp decline.
Falling shipment value, volume and unit prices indicate growing competitive pressure.
To capture more market share, Bangladesh must strengthen synthetic fibre capabilities, speed, flexibility and compliance rather than relying solely on low-cost manufacturing.
